mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2.5% signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 2.5% (20-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0% (20-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and industrial production signal broad economic contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when both HOUST and INDPRO decline (20-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising), higher discount rates and reduced liquidity cause negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods during monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising for 3 months).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts above 1000 thousand units indicate strong consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 5-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST > 1000 (20-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 105 signals manufacturing weakness, reducing corporate profits and causing negative S&P 500 60-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO < 105 (20-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rises in FEDFUNDS and UNRATE signal stagflation, eroding corporate margins and investor confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is rising and UNRATE > 5.0% (20-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.5%), reduced consumer spending causes negative S&P 500 5-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE > 5.5% (20-year rolling window).
